At 3:17 am the bakery was this hush with all the yeast in the air. Marisol was sliding the first loaves into the oven. She saw that worn paperback, The Borrowers. It is always in the wicker basket by the back door, every Thursday for six weeks now instead of the library two blocks over. No name on it. No card, just the book itself, and it smells faintly of rain and woodsmoke.
Tonight, there was a folded note tucked between pages 84 and 85. She wiped her floury hands and opened it. The note read, I can’t make it to the library before closing. Please keep it another week. I like knowing it’s warm.
Marisol looked at the basket, then to the cinnamon rolls cooling on the rack. She chose the one with the most icing. Wrapped it in wax paper. Then she tucked the note back into the book. Set both by the door. And flipped the sign to OPEN, and started the coffee.
